step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture describes a system for virtual software training using AWS AppStream. The primary flow involves users accessing AppStream for the 'Kingdom' application. A separate flow describes the provisioning and customization of the AppStream environment, orchestrated by CloudFormation.Nodes are identified based on distinct icons and labels on the whiteboard and corroborated by the transcript. The external user group is represented by the 'UserConsumerWebMobile' actor. AWS services explicitly shown are AppStream, EC2, Lambda, Systems Manager, CloudFormation, FSx, and RDS.Edges are traced from the visual arrows on the whiteboard, with their purpose clarified by the transcript. Two main flows are identified: one for provisioning and customization, and another for end-user application access.The provisioning flow (flow_id 0) starts with CloudFormation triggering Lambda as a custom resource. Lambda then uses Systems Manager to run commands on an EC2 instance, which acts as the AppStream Image Builder. This EC2 instance configures FSx and then signals CloudFormation upon completion. CloudFormation subsequently provisions AppStream, FSx, and RDS. AppStream also interacts with the EC2 Image Builder during this phase.The end-user access flow (flow_id 1) starts with the user accessing AppStream. AppStream then connects to the EC2 instance (acting as a license server), mounts FSx for project data, and connects to RDS for the database.

graph.name: IHS Market Virtual Software Training
graph.notes: This architecture enables virtual instructor-led training for the Kingdom petrotechnical application. It uses AppStream to deliver the GPU-intensive software, with CloudFormation for automated provisioning and customization of the environment. EC2 serves as both the AppStream Image Builder and the Kingdom license server. FSx provides project storage, and RDS serves as the database.
